meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'without' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's no problem.
This time there's no trick.
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: слава богу = thank God (literally 'glory to God')

examples.trans: Thank God!
No, thank God.

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'century; age' in everyday Russian.
Common masculine noun meaning 'century; age' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The monastery is eight centuries old.
That was in the last century.

examples.text: Наш с вами город очень старый. Почти четыре века здесь были набеги.
examples.trans: Our town is very old. For almost four centuries there were raids here.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'desire, craving' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Sometimes a pregnant woman feels a craving.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть желание.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always desire.
We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: I'm going home.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.
+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to crow'.

examples.trans: Who will crow?

examples.text: И кто тогда будет громко кукарекать?
examples.trans: And who will loudly crow then?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'Mishanya' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть мишаня.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always Mishanya.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'лепый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('absurd, ridiculous').

examples.trans: Ridiculous words.

examples.text: Я сейчас лично проверю эти нелепые слова!
examples.trans: I will personally check these ridiculous words right now!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.trans: I'm thinking about it.
We're talking about the town.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is postponed'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и откладываться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and is postponed on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют откладываться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to is postponed.

meanings.note: Сделать ошибку = to make a mistake. Common feminine noun meaning 'mistake, error' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are many serious mistakes in the case.

examples.text: А прокуратура думает иначе. В деле много грубых ошибок.
examples.trans: The prosecutor's office thinks otherwise. There are many serious mistakes in the case.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'glory be to / hail'.

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'practice / train'.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'practice', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
